\begin{abstract}
We find that a neurosymbolic formalizer (Qwen3-4B trained with GRPO on 500 FOLIO examples) achieves a 93\% prove rate---yet 87\% of proved outputs embed the conclusion among the premises (seed~42), a degenerate shortcut invisible to execution reward.
We introduce \emph{Solver Trace Ablation} (STA), a diagnostic applying leave-one-out component necessity testing to solver inputs; the fraction of necessary components yields the \emph{Intensional Structural Reward} (ISR).
As a diagnostic, ISR exposes a collapse trajectory hidden from prove rate: over 100--1000 GRPO steps, ISR falls to near-zero (e.g., $0.642{\to}0.003$ for seed~42) while prove rate rises dramatically; each seed converges to a qualitatively different hacking mode, yet all three reach 0\% genuine non-hacking by 1000 steps.
A supervised fine-tuning baseline reaches 92.3\% non-hacking on identical data, consistent with GRPO-specific degradation.

\subsection{Cross-Model Generalization: LLaMA-3.2-3B Cold-Start Failure}
\label{app:llama-coldstart}

To probe cross-architecture generalization, we applied the identical GRPO configuration (Table~\ref{tab:hyperparams}) to LLaMA-3.2-3B~\citep{grattafiori2024llama} (3B parameters; execution-only reward, seed~42, $K{=}4$ rollouts, FOLIO training set).
The model produced zero valid Prover9 output across 72 of the planned 500 training steps: reward, policy loss, and gradient norm remained at zero throughout, and training was terminated early.
Manual inspection of generations revealed natural-language text with no first-order logic syntax.
Because $r_{\text{exec}}{=}0$ for all $K$ rollouts on every prompt, the GRPO advantage signal is identically zero and no policy update occurs.

This result establishes a \emph{capability threshold} for GRPO-based formalization: the base model must possess at minimum a rudimentary ability to generate syntactically valid solver input for the RL loop to produce any learning signal.
Qwen3-4B crosses this threshold (non-zero prove rates within the first 10 steps), while LLaMA-3.2-3B does not despite comparable parameter count (3B vs.\ 4B), likely reflecting differences in pretraining data composition rather than model scale \emph{per se}.
An SFT warmstart phase could potentially lift models below this threshold into the regime where RL training produces signal.
